One message of a node's chat. An assistant message may carry a

``applyProposal`` turns into a take.

Edge.description:
``target_node_id`` references ``source_node_id``: the source's selected
output is one of the target's inputs.

EdgeCreate.description:
Fails with ``self_reference``, ``duplicate_edge``, ``cycle``, or
``no_id`` when the source has no ID.

Links follow prompts: creating one appends the source's ID to the
target's prompt (and deleting one removes the mentions).
EdgeCreate.title: EdgeCreate

EditorLimits.description:
What an editor may generate per day (UTC) in one collection, paid by
the owner. Null: no limit of its own (the owner's daily limits still
apply to everything together); 0: none of that kind.
EditorLimits.title: EditorLimits

GenerateRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /api/nodes/{id}/generate``. Empty for now: the node's
saved prompt and params are used, so save before generating.
GenerateRequest.title: GenerateRequest

Invitation.description: An invite to you, as you see it.
Invitation.title: Invitation

Invite.title: Invite

JobInput.description: Exactly what a job was run with, so any take can be reproduced.
JobInput.title: JobInput

Language.description:
The app's language: the UI's, and that of every prompt the backend
writes for the models (the user's own text is sent as written).

Me.description:
Who you're signed in as, and what you pay for today (UTC): everything
generated in your collections, by you or your editors, against your
daily limits (0 means no limit).
Me.title: Me

MediaKind.description: What a node produces, and what kind of thing an output is.

NodeSource.description: Where a node's outputs come from.

NodeUpdate.description:
Partial update: omitted fields are left as they are.

``kind`` can change; when it does and ``params`` is omitted, params reset
to the new kind's defaults. Existing outputs stay attached to the node,
but ``selected_output_id`` is cleared if it no longer matches the kind.
Uploaded nodes cannot change kind or params.
NodeUpdate.title: NodeUpdate

Operation.description:
Which provider call a job makes. Chosen by the backend from the node's
kind and the kinds of its references; the client never picks it.
Operation.title: Operation

Output.description:
One take produced by a node. Text outputs carry ``text``; image and
video outputs carry ``asset``. Uploaded nodes' takes have no job.
Output.title: Output

ProjectGraph.description: Everything the canvas needs to open a project, in one response.

ProjectSummary.description: A project as listed on the landing page.
ProjectSummary.title: ProjectSummary

ResolvedRef.description: A reference as it was used by a job.
ResolvedRef.title: ResolvedRef

RestoreRequest.description: Bring back soft-deleted nodes and edges (undo of a delete).
RestoreRequest.title: RestoreRequest

RestoreResult.description:
What came back: nodes (with their outputs) and edges.

An edge is left deleted if one of its nodes is still deleted, an identical
connection exists again, or it would now make a loop.
RestoreResult.title: RestoreResult

Size.description: Node size in canvas coordinates. Null on a node means "auto".

StepRun.description:
The last run of a step in a project: what it was asked for, and how
it went. A run happens in the background: ``runStep`` answers with the
run ``running``; poll the graph until it is ``done`` or ``failed``.
StepRun.title: StepRun

StepRunRequest.description:
``prompt`` may be empty only for an image or video step fed one-to-one
by text (each text is the prompt). ``count`` is ignored after a
one-to-one step, and required otherwise.
StepRunRequest.title: StepRunRequest

UsageLine.description: Part of today's bill: what one person generated in one collection.

WorkflowSave.description:
Create or replace a workflow (``definition.id`` and ``version`` are

WorkflowSave.title: WorkflowSave

info.description:
Canvas of generation nodes. A node turns a prompt (plus the outputs of the nodes it references) into text, an image or a video.

Every route except /health and the media links needs `Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>`. Projects live in collections, shared by an owner with editors; a change to a project needs its lock (`X-Edit-Session`, see lockProject).
info.title: yuzu-canva API

200.description: The media bytes. Supports HTTP Range for video seeking.

307.description: Redirect to the file in Cloud Storage.

post.description: Turn an answer's proposal into a take of its node (selected).

delete.description: New projects stop getting it; projects made earlier keep their nodes.

patch.description: Rename it. Projects created earlier keep their node names.

200.description: The media bytes. Supports HTTP Range for video seeking.

307.description: Redirect to the file in Cloud Storage.

get.description: The collections you own or edit, most recently changed first.

post.description:
A new collection, yours (its owner), with one workflow: ``workflow``
if given (copy one from another collection), else the built-in one.

delete.description:
Owner only. Deletes it for everyone, with every project in it, its
workflows, assets, members and invites, and their files. Usage records
stay (they still count today).

patch.description:
Rename it or change its instruction (new projects start with a copy).
409 ``edit_conflict`` if someone saved since ``version``.

get.description:
The collection's assets, oldest first (the order new projects lay
them out).

post.description:
Upload one image (PNG, JPEG, WebP) or video (MP4, MOV) with a name.

Multipart fields ``file`` and ``name``. The name is required and unique
in the collection (409 ``duplicate_name``). Every project created in the
collection from now on starts with it as a node.

get.description: Invites waiting to be accepted, newest first.

post.description:
Owner only: invite an email as an editor, with their daily limits
here. They see it after signing in (no email is sent) and accept it to
get in; it expires after 30 days. Inviting the same email again renews
it. 409 if they're already a member. They also need to be on the app's
allowlist to sign in at all.

get.description:
The owner first, then editors, each with their limits and what they
generated here today.

delete.description:
The owner removes an editor, or an editor leaves (their own user ID).
What they made stays. The owner can't leave (409).

patch.description: Owner only: set an editor's daily limits here.

get.description:
The collection's projects, most recently updated first, with counts,
a cover, and who else is editing each right now.

post.description:
Create a project. It runs on the collection's active workflow and
starts with one uploaded node per collection asset, down the left side
of its canvas.

get.description: The collection's workflows, oldest first; one is active.

post.description:
A new workflow, not active yet (422 if two steps share a key). To
copy one from another collection, send its definition.

delete.description:
Soft delete: ``restoreDeleted`` can bring it back (undo). Workflow
edges can't be deleted (409 ``workflow_locked``).

get.description: Invites to you (by your sign-in email), newest first.

post.description: Join the collection as an editor.
Cancel a queued or running job. Fails (409) with ``job_finished``.

delete.description: Remove it from the library. Nodes placed from it are unaffected.

post.description:
Put a material on the canvas as an uploaded node.

The node is named after the file (made unique), and its single take is the
file, already selected, so it can be used as another node's input at once.

get.description:
Who you're signed in as (401 if not, 403 if not on the allowlist),
and what you pay for today (everything generated in your collections,
by anyone) against your limits.

delete.description:
Deletes the node and every edge touching it; cancels its running jobs.

The delete is soft: ``restoreDeleted`` brings the node back with its
takes (undo) until it is purged a day later. Downstream nodes keep their
own outputs; prompts that mention its ID keep the text (unlinked).

patch.description:
Move, resize, rename, edit the prompt or params, or pick a take.

``selected_output_id`` must be one of this node's outputs. A name must be
unique in the project (409 ``duplicate_name``); null or blank removes it.

post.description:
Ask the model about a text node; returns your message and its answer.

The model sees the project instruction (for a workflow node, and its
step), the current version and the chat so far. When it suggests a new
version, the answer's ``proposal`` holds it whole; ``applyProposal``
turns it into a take. Nothing is saved if the model fails (502).

Queue a generation from the node's saved prompt, params and references.

Each reference resolves to the source node's ``selected_output_id``.
Fails (409) with ``missing_ref_output``, ``unsupported_ref``,
``too_many_refs``, ``job_in_progress`` or
``not_generatable`` (an uploaded node); 429 ``quota_exceeded`` past a
limit; 503 ``generation_off``. Poll ``getJob`` (or the graph) for
progress.

get.description: Every take of the node, newest first.

post.description: A text take written by hand; it becomes the selected take.

delete.description:
Owner only; even while someone is editing it (their next request
gets 404). Deletes the project with its nodes, edges, jobs, outputs,
assets and their files.

get.description: The whole canvas: project, nodes, edges, outputs and active jobs.

post.description:
Make the target node reference the source node (it needs an ID).

This appends the source's ID to the target's prompt, since links exist
exactly when the prompt mentions the source.

Fails (409) with ``self_reference``, ``duplicate_edge`` or ``cycle``.
Both nodes must be in the project (else 404). Kind compatibility is
checked at generate time, not here, since a node's kind can change.

delete.description: Release the lock, if this tab holds it.

parameters.name: X-Edit-Session

schema.description: This browser tab's own random ID, the same for all its requests.
schema.title: X-Edit-Session

post.description:
Take or renew the lock for this tab: only the tab holding it may
change the project. It lasts 60 s; renew it (call again) every 20 s
while the project is open, and release it on leaving.

409 ``project_locked`` while someone else holds it (``context``:
``holder_email``, ``holder_is_you``). With ``take_over``, you take it
from your own other tab (never from someone else). Any change to the
project also takes the lock if it's free.

parameters.description: This browser tab's own random ID, the same for all its requests.
parameters.name: X-Edit-Session

schema.description: This browser tab's own random ID, the same for all its requests.
schema.title: X-Edit-Session

get.description: The project's uploaded images and videos, newest first.

post.description:
Upload one image (PNG, JPEG, WebP) or video (MP4, MOV), multipart field ``file``.

The type comes from the file's content, not its name. Fails with
``unsupported_media`` (415) or ``too_large`` (413).

Undo deletes: bring back soft-deleted nodes (with their takes) and edges.

Deleted items are kept for a day, then purged when the API starts.

Start running a step; returns the graph with the run ``running``.

It finishes in the background: poll ``getProjectGraph`` until the step's
run is ``done`` (its nodes replaced, image and video nodes generating)
or ``failed`` (``error`` says why; the old nodes are untouched). 409 if
the step is already running.

The prompt, the project instruction and the nodes the prompt mentions
(by ID) go to a text model, which writes ``count`` results (a text
step: its nodes' text) or prompts (an image or video step: one node
each, generated right away, with the mentioned nodes as references).
After a one-to-one step, there is one result per node of that step
(``count`` is ignored), each made from its own input; an image or video
step fed by text uses each text as its prompt directly.

get.description:
Your settings: the language of the UI and of every prompt the
backend writes for the models.

put.description:
Replace a workflow (its version goes up). Editing the active one
changes it for every project in the collection, so it's refused (409)
while a step runs there; 409 ``edit_conflict`` if someone saved since
``base_version``.

post.description:
Every project in the collection runs on this workflow from now on;
their steps keep their results by step key (steps it doesn't have are
hidden until a workflow with them is active again). 409 while a step
runs in the collection.
